LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.1 INTENSIVE LISTENING: TRANSCRIPTION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription, part of Strand 7 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we transcribe oral texts accurately? 2. Why do we transcribe texts in indigenous languages?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. outline target words related to the theme from an oral text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. transcribe a short listening paragraph from a digital device for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the role of transcription in the growth of Indigenous Languages.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. outline target words related to the theme from an oral text for comprehension,

   Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. transcribe a short listening paragraph from a digital device for effective communication,

   Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the role of transcription in the growth of Indigenous Languages.

   Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an oral text on talents and gifts and pick out specific talents and gifts,

2. write a paragraph by transcribing an audio-recorded story based on the theme and share with peers,

3. peer review each other’s transcription for accuracy,

4. organise the transcribed work in a portfolio,

5. work with peers to discuss talents and gifts they have seen or possess. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an oral text on talents and gifts and pick out specific talents and gifts,
2. write a paragraph by transcribing an audio-recorded story based on the theme and share with peers,
3. peer review each other’s transcription for accuracy,
4. organise the transcribed work in a portfolio,
5. work with peers to discuss talents and gifts they have seen or possess. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Intensive listening: Transcription together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner engages in constructive dialogue when discussing the various talents and

gifts.

• Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner reflects on their own and other’s work when peer reviewing each

other’s transcriptions.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is developed as the learner commits to organising the transcribed work in a portfolio.

• Social Justice: This is enhanced as the learner accords peers equal opportunities to contribute when picking out

specific talents and gifts from the oral text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

ICT is promoted as the learner writes a paragraph by transcribing an audio-recorded story based on the theme and shares it

with peers.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the skills of intensive listening to their learning in Kiswahili.
